schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT A1.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (A1.FIRST_LOGIN + 1) = A2.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/ COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS A1 JOIN ACTIVITY AS A2 ON A1.PLAYER_ID = A2.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY A1.FIRST_LOGIN
q2: WITH IN_DT AS ( SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY A GROUP BY 1 ) , RETENT AS ( SELECT DISTINCT I.PLAYER_ID, FIRST_LOGIN FROM IN_DT I INNER JOIN ACTIVITY A ON A.PLAYER_ID = I.PLAYER_ID AND DATE_ADD(I.FIRST_LOGIN, INTERVAL 1 DAY) = A.EVENT_DATE ) SELECT I.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT I.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT R.PLAYER_ID)/COUNT(DISTINCT I.PLAYER_ID),2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM IN_DT I LEFT JOIN RETENT R ON R.PLAYER_ID = I.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC

explanation: Both queries aim to calculate the day-1 retention rate, which is the proportion of players who return to play the game the day after their first login. They achieve this by identifying the first login date for each player and then counting how many of these players have an activity on the day immediately following their first login.
